approved: Customs Tariff Amendment (Cost of Living Support) Bill 2022
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would raise the thresholds at which people start paying the Medicare levy and surcharge.
The thresholds would be increased in line with movements in the consumer price index (CPI).
The changes would apply from the 2021–22 income year and are estimated to reduce government revenue by $90 million over the forward estimates.
Raises the Medicare levy low-income thresholds for individuals, families and those eligible for the seniors and pensioners tax offset (SAPTO).
Raises the Medicare levy surcharge low-income threshold.
Aligns the threshold increases with CPI movements.
Individuals and families whose incomes are below the new thresholds, particularly those eligible for SAPTO.

The bill halves the excise rate on domestically produced petrol and diesel from 44.2 to 22.1 cents per litre for six months from 30 March to 28 September 2022, citing the Russian invasion of Ukraine and cost-of-living pressures, with the ACCC monitoring to ensure benefits are passed on.
Customs Tariff Amendment (Cost of Living Support) Act 2022
